name: Remotion Blur Scale Text Morph
use_when: One short word or concept should transform into another with a soft premium feel.
A title transition needs more physical texture than a plain crossfade.
The outgoing and incoming words can share a controlled layout.
avoid_when: Both words must remain readable throughout the transition.
The words have very different lengths and no design plan for the shared position.
The scene already has enough blur, glow, or motion competing with the text.

timeline_pattern.pattern: outgoing_word_layer -> incoming_word_layer_absolute -> shared_progress -> outgoing_blur_scale_opacity_out -> incoming_blur_scale_opacity_in -> readable_hold
timeline_pattern.layer_rule: Both words share a container so the morph feels like one text event.
timeline_pattern.progress_rule: Use one progress value to drive opposite opacity, blur, and scale states.
timeline_pattern.hold_rule: Show each word clearly before and after the morph.

motion.rule: Blur and scale should imply transformation without hiding the final message.

keyframe_values.morph_duration: Around 30 frames can work for a clear title morph at 30fps; shorten only when the words are very simple.
keyframe_values.blur_limit: Keep blur below the point where the text becomes a muddy block; values around the mid-20 px range are already strong.
keyframe_values.scale_out: Outgoing text can scale up slightly while fading/blurred; incoming text can start smaller and sharpen to normal size.

sound.rule: Use a soft swell, shimmer, or no SFX; avoid hard impacts unless the morph is a beat accent.

captions.rule: Do not use morphing text as the only caption for important spoken content.

color.rule: Use consistent color roles across both words unless the concept shift intentionally changes tone.

implementation.ffmpeg: Pre-render the morph from Remotion or use two drawtext layers with alpha and blur approximations for simple tests.
implementation.remotion: Stack outgoing and incoming text in one relative container; drive filter blur, transform scale, and opacity from a shared interpolated progress.
implementation.blender: Use two text objects with animated opacity, scale, and compositor blur.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Duplicate text layers and keyframe blur, opacity, and scale in opposite directions.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Nest two Essential Graphics layers and animate blur, scale, and opacity, or use AE/Remotion for cleaner timing.

common_mistakes: Letting the mid-transition blur cover faces, proof, UI, or captions.
Morphing long phrases that need plain readability.
Not holding the incoming word after it sharpens.
Using blur values that create compression dirt.
Changing font role or alignment accidentally between the two words.
qc: Outgoing word is readable before the morph starts.
Incoming word is readable after the morph settles.
Mid-transition blur does not hide key visual information.
Font, alignment, and color choices feel intentional across both words.
The morph duration matches the scene pace.
